Subject: Volume estimate & baseline pricing question

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to share a short projection so they can understand committed spend options. Attached is a simple monthly projection for peak holiday and baseline months.

High-level ask: can you share a baseline hosted-API rate card for the following committed tiers so we can model cost/ROI?
- 500M tokens / month
- 2B tokens / month
- 6B tokens / month

Also: do you offer any smoothing of usage across months for billing, or is commit enforced per calendar month? And what kind of unit discounts are available for an initial 12-month commit vs a rolling monthly commitment?

We're early in the procurement process; procurement@acmeretail.com is on cc. Legal may follow with a few contract questions.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Head of AI Product
Acme Retail

Attachment: Acme_Monthly_Volume_Projection.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-07-22T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Volume estimate & baseline pricing question

Sophie — thanks for the projection, looks straightforward. Quick answers up front:
- We support both calendar-month commits and a 12-month committed token plan. For 12-month commits we typically offer deeper tiered discounts and the option to smooth billing across months (you can carry forward up to 20% of unused committed tokens in a quarter).
- We can provide a provisional rate card for the three breakpoints you listed and a recommended staging plan for ramping during holiday.

I've attached a draft rate card and a short note on breakpoints. Key trade-offs to call out: higher commits give lower per-token price but require minimum monthly billing; large spikes above commit are billed at an overage rate that we can cap for enterprise customers with an SLO-based overage protection.

Next steps: if you confirm which tier you want to model (monthly vs 12-month commit) I can loop in finance to put a formal quote.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — PDF looks useful. For modeling purposes we want two scenarios:

Scenario A (Conservative): 500M tokens/month, 12-month commit
Scenario B (Aggressive): 6B tokens/month, 12-month commit with a Q4 holiday spike + smoothing

Two specific asks before we move to quote:
1) Can you show a simple effective $/1k-token price after discounts and any volume rebates?
2) For Scenario B, what is the breakpoint for the next discount after 6B (i.e., where does per-token drop meaningfully)?

Legal will also want to confirm data handling for hosted API (we don't send PII) and retention windows; I'll let them follow up separately.

Sophie

Hi Sophie — looping in to help with the numbers (I'm the AE working with Ben on this account). We ran quick math with finance for two illustrative effective prices (these are illustrative, final quote will be by finance):

Scenario A (500M/mo, 12mo commit):
- Base hosted API list: $0.03 per 1k tokens
- 12mo commit discount: 20% -> effective $0.024/1k tokens
- Quarterly volume rebate for meeting 95%+ utilization: additional 5% rebate applied retroactively
- Effective modeled price (w/rebate): ~$0.0228/1k tokens

Scenario B (6B/mo, 12mo commit):
- Base list: $0.03/1k
- Tiered discount ladder: 6B+ -> 35% off => $0.0195/1k
- Additional performance rebate for smoothing + autoscaling engagement: up to 5% -> ~$0.0185/1k
- Next meaningful breakpoint after 6B is 20B/month where discount moves to ~45% (we can show a multi-year slide to get there)

Billing cadence options: monthly invoicing with committed monthly minimum, or quarterly invoicing with smoothing. We can include a true-up at quarter end.

If these ballpark numbers look viable, I'll ask Marcus (finance) to produce a formal quote and include invoice cadence options and overage cap language.

Thanks — Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmeretail.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-07-24T11:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Volume estimate & baseline pricing question

Sophie — Marcus from Finance here. I put together a compact discount ladder and a few commercial guardrails: see bullets below and attached redlines.

- Breakpoints (committed tokens / month):
  * 0.5B -> base $0.03/1k tokens -> 20% off for 12mo commit -> $0.024/1k
  * 2B -> 28% off -> $0.0216/1k
  * 6B -> 35% off -> $0.0195/1k
  * 20B -> 45% off -> $0.0165/1k

- Overage handling: we bill overages at 1.5x the committed rate for usage within a 10% monthly buffer; customers may purchase a temporary burst add-on to cap overage charges. For enterprise customers we can cap month-over-month overage charges at a negotiated dollar amount.

- Billing & smoothing: we support carry-forward of up to 20% committed tokens within the same quarter and quarterly true-up. Invoice options: monthly or quarterly.

- Commercial term: 12-month minimum for discounted tiers. We can provide a 60-day early-termination schedule with staggered repayment of the discount if needed.

- Audit & evidence: we can provide token-level usage reports and a monthly CSV export. SOC2 summary and data retention info will be attached for Legal.

Next step: I can produce a formal quote with line items, one for Scenario A and one for Scenario B, including a modeled annual spend and a suggested smoothing schedule. If you want an overage cap for Scenario B, tell me a target $ cap and I can bake it into the quote.

Attachment: draft-MSA-redlines.pdf (PDF)

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Manager, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmeretail.com>

2) Please include the performance rebate clause language you mentioned (what qualifies for the rebate) so finance can model net effective pricing.
3) Legal will confirm the SOC2 and data retention summary but flagged the hosted API data treatement paragraph; I'll have them follow-up with redlines if any.

If you can get a formal quote and the modeled $/1k effective price for both scenarios by Monday EOD (PST) we'll present to our CFO on Tuesday.

I'll also send a short DocuSign request once the quote is ready.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Sophie
Head of AI Product, Acme Retail
